chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

No Muslim visits his Muslim brother for the sake of Allah and for Allah's sake, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls out to him: 'O visitor! You have done well, and Paradise is made sweet/better for you.'

key_terms.طِبْتَ: you have done well / you are pure

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a Muslim brother for the sake of God?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight 'ziarat li-l-lah' (visiting for God's sake) as a profound act of worship that transcends mere social courtesy. The divine call 'You have become pure' (ṭibta) signifies the purification of the soul through sincere connection with the brethren, a concept central to Shia ethics of community bonding. This direct address by Allah underscores the high spiritual status of the visitor, linking interpersonal kindness directly to eternal reward.
